mechanism_narrative: The significant week-on-week rebound in RETAIL_REC mobility observed in the most recent period indicates a sustained recovery trend, which will lead to higher overall retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the average of the last 28 days, despite the recent positive shift.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in WORKPLACES mobility, exceeding 5 percentage points week-on-week, signals a strong return to office routines that will drive increased retail and recreation visits during lunch breaks and after work over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an increase in the next two weeks following a week where WORKPLACES rose by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility and significant increase in TRANSIT station visits indicates a strong shift away from home-bound activities towards out-of-home engagement, boosting retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases despite RESIDENTIAL falling and TRANSIT rising concurrently over the observation period.

mechanism_narrative: As the summer holiday period concludes and people return to urban centers, the observed rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS mobility indicates a general re-engagement with local amenities, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase, or even declines, during the post-summer period despite increases in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, exceeding 4 percentage points, suggests a broader return of daily routines and local activity, which will spill over into retail and recreation within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the immediate week following a week where GROCERY_PHARM mobility surged by more than 4 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent rise in WORKPLACES and PARKS mobility indicates a dual trend of returning to work and maintaining leisure activities outside the home, suggesting a robust increase in overall out-of-home movement that will benefit retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat despite both WORKPLACES and PARKS showing positive week-on-week changes.

mechanism_narrative: The broad-based and significant rebound across multiple mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, GROCERY_PHARM, TRANSIT, WORKPLACES) in the most recent week signifies a strong underlying momentum for increased out-of-home activity, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: The average RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the average of the last 28 days, despite the observed broad rebound across multiple categories.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past three weeks, coupled with the end of summer, indicates a clear shift towards more time spent outside the home, directly contributing to increased foot traffic in retail and recreation venues over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL shows a consistent decline over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next two weeks, even with a continued and consistent decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility.
